_why: Milestone 0.4. rule-diff.sh reports every per-rule count change between the
last release and this build. Reporting is not accountability: a drop and a
correct narrowing look identical in that output, and the only thing telling
them apart was whoever happened to read the job summary.
This file is the other half. Every rule whose count DROPS must have an entry
here saying why. An unexplained drop fails the job; so does an entry that no
longer describes a real drop, because a ledger nothing validates rots into
The baseline is the last released nox, so entries accumulate between releases
and are cleared when one is cut. `nox_release` records which release they are
written against: if it does not match the tag rule-diff resolved, the ledger
is stale as a whole and says so rather than silently passing.

classifications.duplicate-retired: a second rule reported the same condition; one ID was retired into the other, which carries the alias
classifications.applicability-narrowed: the rule does not apply to this subject or resource kind, and now says so
classifications.sanitizer-recognized: the value reaching the sink is neutralized for this vulnerability class
classifications.refined-away: a cheaper semantic fact refutes the candidate the pattern generated
classifications.rule-removed: the rule was deleted outright; no survivor reports the condition
classifications.context-narrowed: the rule's context requirement is now measured in characters as well as lines, so a keyword far away on the same physical line no longer qualifies as context
classifications.keyword-tokenized: the rule's vendor keyword must now be a token; it used to match as a bare substring, so it could be supplied by an accident inside opaque data or by an ordinary English word
classifications.format-bound: the rule now requires the vendor's real credential format; the value it matched is issued by that vendor but is not a credential
classifications.binding-required: the vendor name must now BIND the value through an assignment; sitting adjacent to a generic token is not evidence that the token is that vendor's credential

entries.reason: SEC-082 claims a hardcoded bearer token. A value built only from short words and numbers that carries a test marker, opens with a translated "your", or uses only credential vocabulary is a placeholder, not a token. On the corpus: vercel-ai-mistral 7 -> 0, every one `authorization: 'Bearer test-api-key'` in a *.test.ts file. On the seven-repo benchmark SEC-082 drops 274 lines, read grouped by value: test-api-key 86, test-key 32, test-token 32, custom-token 20, mock-auth-token 18, token 14, secret 11, mock-api-key 9, TEST_TOKEN 8, and smaller groups of the same kind; nothing is added and no real credential is among them. A random value (a JWT, sk_test_51H...) is never word-composed, and TestDescriptiveValuesArePlaceholders asserts it stays reported.

DATA-001 is CWE-359, private personal information. Two refutations: a role mailbox (support@, hello@, noreply@, matched on the whole local part) names a function rather than a person, and the password@host of a connection URL is URL userinfo, not an e-mail address. On the corpus: chronos 2 -> 1, the dropped line `mysql://user:pw@db.local:6603/?namespace=tenant_a` in internal/store/mysql/mysql_test.go (URL userinfo); the kept one is in .goreleaser.yaml. On the seven-repo benchmark DATA 369 -> 55, all 314 drops read: support@crewai.com 156, hello@neatlogs.com 152, deploy@/noreply@/support@unstructured.io/git@github.com 4, postgresql://…:password@ 2. Personal addresses (a gmail address, jane@…) are still reported; #733 landed while rule-diff exited 1 on a crash and passed, which is why this entry arrives with the harness fix.

SEC-161 (high-entropy string) fired inside ciphertext a model API issued and takes back: Anthropic's thinking-block signature and web-search encrypted_index, OpenAI's reasoning encrypted_content, Gemini's thoughtSignature. A match in the string value of one of those JSON keys is now refuted. On the corpus: anthropic-sdk-python 58 -> 50 and vercel-ai-anthropic 9 -> 0, recorded responses under tests/ and __fixtures__/. On the seven-repo benchmark the refutation removes 67 findings, all read and all under those four keys (SEC-161 32, SEC-048 21, SEC-055 14); the same token under any other key is still reported.

TAINT-002 claims command injection. For Python, the flag "taint is in the first argument" was set whenever the first argument held any variable, so a call whose tainted value sat only in a later argument -- env=os.environ -- was judged as if the command itself were tainted. It is now set from the taint state at the sink. On the corpus: certbot 3 -> 1. The two dropped are acme_server.py:191 `subprocess.Popen(command, ..., env=env)` and tools/venv.py:137 `subprocess.check_output(cmd, env=env, shell=shell)`, both with env from os.environ and an untainted command; a third drop, apache-conf-test-pebble.py:22 env via `environ`, sits on a line whose argv-to-command flow is still reported (the kept finding). On the seven-repo benchmark the same shape drops three in llama_index's dev CLI (os.environ.copy() passed as env= to an argv subprocess.run). Nothing is added.
